correctness.rationale: For every n, the four-state digit recurrence and proved closed eight-pair adjacency set imply that all factors occur among at most 8 times 2^ceil(log2 n) substituted two-block windows, and every candidate window genuinely occurs. For binary words of length n, all scattered counts through length two reduce algebraically to (ones weight, index sum), as shown by #10=w(n-1)-T-C(w,2). Enumeration uses exact 64-bit sums, a correctly updated moment recurrence, a justified n<=4096 cutoff, and packed pair identifiers without collision. A second program independently computes Rudin–Shapiro digits from their base-two definition and matches all 4096 data rows and all dyadic weight counts, with an independent exact cover of the same infinite factor language. Neither finite experiment nor log alone is offered as an infinite claim; infinite statements rely on the proven cover and coding.

value.rationale: The Rudin–Shapiro word is a classical four-state automatic sequence and 2-binomial complexity is a natural refinement of its well-studied abelian complexity. The exact table covers every length up to a nonarbitrary full substitution scale 2^12, with a complete weight distribution at all dyadic scales, in contrast to isolated small computations; e.g. length 4096 has only 191 weights but 24783 distinct scattered-subsequence classes. The paper supplies a structural exact factor-cover reduction for every length, not just a data dump. These exact values and the striking nonmonotone dyadic structure are mathematically motivated benchmark information for future structural formulas. No general asymptotic or conjectural extension is claimed.
